[HERMIT HUT] — A gnarled tree-root cottage sunk into a forest hillside, walls of packed mud reinforced with woven hazel-wands, ceiling low enough to brush with an outstretched hand. A stone-lipped firepit dominates one corner, hung with drying herb-bundles on iron hooks. A sleeping pallet covered in moth-eaten wolfskin sits beneath a single oval window of thick green glass. A battered mortar and blackened spoon rest on the sill.

[GLOWING CAVE] — A drow matriarch's private grotto carved into pale violet limestone, walls threaded with bioluminescent crystal veins that pulse faintly like slow breath. The floor is worn smooth by decades of bare feet. A low stone shelf serves as both desk and altar, scattered with carved obsidian tokens and stoppered vials. A silk hammock hangs between two natural pillars, its fabric dark as deep water.

[SWAMP SHACK] — A fenwitch's stilt-house rising from black water on crooked cypress legs, walls of overlapping reed-thatch chinked with grey clay. The single room smells of peat and rotting bark. A cast-iron cauldron squats on a clay hearth-stone, bubbling something green. A string of crow skulls and dried cattails hangs across the low doorway. A cracked hand-mirror leans against the far wall, its frame wound with copper wire.

[TOWER-TOP OBSERVATORY] — A wizard's upper chamber open to the sky on three sides through tall lancet arches, their stone lips worn smooth by wind and rain. The curved floor is inlaid with a brass celestial chart. A heavy brass-ringed telescope squats on a pivot-mount at the room's center. Loose star-charts weighted with river stones cover a tilted reading-desk. A threadbare cloak hangs from one arch-stone, forgotten or left deliberately.

[MOUNTAIN CABIN] — An alchemist's ledge-cabin notched into a granite cliff face, three walls of rough-cut stone and one wall of the cliff itself, raw and damp. Ceiling-beams are low, smoke-stained, hung with bundles of sulfur-yellow crystals. A long worktable dominates the room, crowded with retorts, sealed jars of coloured powders, and a single oil lamp casting amber shadows. Boot-shaped scorch marks blacken the floor beneath the table.

[SUBTERRANEAN MUSHROOM-GROVE] — A gnomish seer's home hollowed beneath an ancient oak's root-network, walls living root-wood lacquered with pine resin. The floor is carpeted in soft glowing fungi, blue-white, small as thumbnails. A carved root-bench holds a collection of smooth river stones, each painted with an eye. A passage-opening in one wall is curtained with woven root-fiber. A tin cup and half-eaten heel of bread sit on the bench's arm.

[COASTAL SHACK] — A sea-seer's driftwood hut jammed between two boulders on a rocky shore, its outer walls planks of bleached grey driftwood roped together with kelp-fiber. Inside, the ceiling is low, hung with net-draped glass fishing-floats glowing soft green. A stone basin in one corner holds salt water and a scrying-stone. A narrow rope-and-plank bed is wedged beneath the single shutter-window facing the grey sea.

[TREEHOUSE] — A wood-elf waykeeper's platform-home sixty feet up in a great ash, floor of living branch-wood sealed with amber resin, walls open on two sides to the canopy. Thin carved-wood screens on the open sides filter light into leaf-patterns. A woven-grass sleeping mat is rolled into one corner beside a clay water-jug. A single carved rune-post at the platform's center holds a lantern of green witchlight. Acorn-caps and pressed leaves litter the floor.

[WIZARD STUDY] — A lorekeeper's private archive alcove off a vast tower library, stone-vaulted ceiling barely six feet at its highest, shelves recessed directly into the curved walls. A single leaded-glass window no larger than a shield overlooks a courtyard. A reading-chair upholstered in worn red leather sits under the window, a half-open tome balanced on its arm. Ink-stained fingerprints mark the window-sill. A mug of cold tea sits forgotten on the floor.

[CASTLE PRIVATE CHAMBER] — A royal mage's quarters in a curtain-tower, walls of dressed limestone hung with a single large star-map on stitched linen, yellowing at its corners. The floor is bare stone except for a small, intensely patterned wool rug beside the bed. A writing-desk against the outer wall holds a mass of papers weighed by a carved-stone hand. A narrow arrow-loop window has been widened and fitted with leaded glass.

[TRAVELER'S TENT] — A caravan-mage's pavilion of layered oilcloth panels in deep burgundy and brown, the poles carved with small interlocking serpent-spirals. Inside, the floor is covered in overlapping woven wool mats. A small folding table holds a crystal ball nested in a ring-stand and three tallow candles. Tapestry wall-hangings cover all interior fabric walls, their scenes worn soft with age. A battered wooden chest serves as both seat and wardrobe, its latch replaced with a leather strap.

[MAGICAL BOOKSHOP] — A curiosity-dealer's back-room hidden behind a curtain of hanging brass keys, walls rough brick softened by decades of damp, every surface covered by mismatched shelving. Stacked tomes lean against rolled scroll-cases on the floor. A single oil-lamp on a pile of books serves as the only light. A moth-eaten armchair sits in the corner, its cushion permanently compressed. A half-eaten apple and an uncapped ink-bottle sit on the nearest shelf beside a cracked glass sphere.

[SUBTERRANEAN SANCTUM] — A half-orc hexblade's underground retreat carved beneath a ruined keep's foundations, reached through a trapdoor in a root-cellar. Walls are old cut-stone, lime-washed once and now patchy. A cracked mirror mounted in one wall reflects a globe of blue witchlight floating unsupported in the room's center. A weapons-stand holding a single notched sword stands near a pallet-bed with rough wool blankets. A tin plate with dried gravy and a leather-bound ledger sit side by side on the floor.

[CARAVAN INTERIOR] — A traveling magician's caravan wagon, its arched interior lined with cedar-plank shelves packed with tied bundles, scroll-cases, and glass curiosities. Lanterns on gimbaled iron brackets swing gently with the road's memory. A fold-down bunk is latched to one wall, a patchwork quilt bunched at its foot. A small hinged table holds a spread of worn tarot-style cards mid-reading, a candle stub melted low beside them.

[MAGICAL BOOKSHOP BACK ROOM] — The after-hours back room of a cluttered magical scrollery, its low ceiling crammed with hanging scroll-tubes and bundled vellum. Tall leaning shelves of books occupy every wall to the rafters. A small clerk's desk holds an ink-set and an open ledger dense with cramped figures. One greasy tallow candle burns in a saucer. A traveling cloak is draped over a stool; muddy boots stand beside the back door.

[SUBTERRANEAN SPACE] — A stone-cut underground sanctum beneath a ruined keep, reached by a rope-guided descent through a floor-hatch. Its low ceiling is natural rock; its walls are cut stone fitted with iron torch-brackets, most empty. A single burning torch illuminates a floor covered in overlapping chalk ritual circles half-rubbed out. A bedroll is tucked under a stone bench. A locked iron strongbox serves as a table for a clay bowl and candle.

[TOWER-TOP CHAMBER] — An astronomer-mage's observation room at a tower's summit, its circular stone walls interrupted by four arched window-slits fitted with removable lens-panels. Star-maps painted directly onto plaster cover every inch between the windows. A rotating brass instrument on a central tripod points toward the highest window. A narrow sleeping cot is pushed against the curved wall, its blanket embroidered with constellation-lines. A cold supper sits forgotten on the floor.

[FOREST CABIN] — An herbalist's woodland cabin, its squared-log walls chinked with grey moss, its roof steeply pitched and thick with living turf. Inside: a single deep-silled window of rippled greenish glass; a long work-table cluttered with sorting trays, bundles of drying roots, and a worn wooden mortar. A peg-rail holds two cloaks and a wicker basket. A narrow bedframe with a straw tick occupies the far corner beside a small cold hearth.

HERMIT'S FOREST HUT — Wattle-and-daub walls packed with dried herb-bundles, low beam ceiling hung with braided garlic and crow feathers, plank floor worn smooth by decades of bare feet, a single oilskin window casting amber light. A stone basin sits beside a battered cauldron over cold ash; a moth-eaten cloak hangs on an iron peg. Every surface is a shelf.

DROW'S CRYSTAL CAVE — Raw obsidian walls threaded with veins of phosphorescent violet crystal that pulse faintly like slow breath, ceiling a rough dome of natural stone, floor smoothed and inlaid with a mosaic of crushed quartz. A hammock-bed of spider-silk spans one corner; a low stone table holds inkpots and unfinished glyphs. The cave hums with its owner's ambient magic.

SWAMP-HAG'S STILT-HOUSE — Warped cypress planks form walls hung with bottled eyes and knotted reed-charms, the floor elevated on rot-dark stilts above black water, ceiling so low it grazes a tall visitor's crown. Gaps between boards serve as windows, admitting fog and frog-song. A cracked iron pot hangs over a sunken fire-pit; a straw sleeping pallet is tucked beneath a shelf of skulls.

ALCHEMIST'S MOUNTAIN-LEDGE CABIN — Stone-block walls mortared against high-altitude wind, ceiling beams crusted with frost that never fully thaws, a single deep-set arched window overlooking a sheer drop into cloud. A battered alembic dominates the central worktable beside rows of labeled clay flasks. A fur-lined bedroll is shoved against the far wall; a rune-carved hearthstone provides the only warmth.

WOOD-ELF CANOPY TREEHOUSE — Walls of living woven-branch latticework, floor a platform of lashed planks settled between three enormous boughs, ceiling open to the canopy with a waxed-leather rain-panel rigged above. Bioluminescent moss clings to the branch-walls. A carved-wood sleeping ledge holds a grass-stuffed mattress; wind-chimes of acorn-cap and bone hang from every low branch.

WIZARD'S TOWER READING-NOOK — A small vaulted alcove off the main tower stair, curved limestone walls lined floor-to-ceiling with mismatched bookshelves, a leaded-glass lancet window overlooking rooftops below. The floor rug is threadbare at the center from a single habitual chair. A cracked mug holds quills; an open grimoire is face-down on the armrest, spine thoroughly broken.

UNDERDARK MUSHROOM-GROVE SANCTUM — A shallow cave whose floor is overtaken by enormous shelf-fungi serving as table, chair, and shelf alike, ceiling draped in glowing spore-silk that drifts like underwater kelp. The walls are living fungal colonies in amber, blue, and pale green. A stone basin filled with luminous water serves as mirror and wash-bowl; scattered across one broad mushroom-cap are bone-carved rune-tiles.

SEA-CAVE HERMIT'S HOME — A coastal cave mouth partially walled with stacked driftwood and sea-mortar, floor of wave-polished pebble laid with a salvaged rope-mat, ceiling vaulted and salt-crusted, the sea-entrance framed by hanging dried kelp curtains. A driftwood shelf holds wax-sealed jars of tide-gathered curios. A hammock of knotted fishing-net stretches between two stone pillars; a seer's scrying-bowl sits half-full of dark brine.

FENWITCH'S REED-HUT — Tightly bundled reed walls that whisper in wind, floor raised on sunken piles above a reed-fringed canal, ceiling barely overhead and hung with drying marsh-herbs in dense ropes. A square hole cut in the east wall serves as window, its shutter a single hinged board. A narrow sleeping pallet is curtained off with hempen cloth; a clay fire-pot smolders in the center.

CARAVAN MAGICIAN'S WAGON INTERIOR — Wooden paneled walls painted in faded celestial motifs, curved barrel-vault ceiling hung with pendant charms and bundled scrolls, floor covered in overlapping woven wool mats. A fold-down writing shelf doubles as a sleeping board when lowered. One round port-window with thick greenish glass admits traveling light. A locked brass chest under the board is clearly the most important thing here.

DWARVEN RUNE-SCRIBE'S STONE ALCOVE — Hewn granite walls covered edge-to-edge in carved runes inlaid with copper and cold-iron, ceiling vaulted in a low arch, floor of black flagstone polished by iron-shod boots. A single tallow candle-cluster mounted in a wall-sconce provides warm tunneled light. A heavy oak stool sits before a stone desk; one corner holds a narrow sleeping shelf with a rough wool blanket.

HERBALIST'S WOODLAND CABIN — Rough-hewn log walls chinked with moss and clay, raftered ceiling thick with hanging herb-clusters and wax-paper seed-packets tied with twine, floor of packed earth covered by a hooked rag-rug. Two small oilpaper windows frame the door. A worktable scarred by years of chopping holds mortar and pestle, and a leatherbound herb-catalogue left open to a dog-eared page on nightshade variants.
